To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the current socio-technical design approaches are not suitable for use in the development of complex, safety-critical socio-technical systems; (2) socio-technical approaches to systems development are best understood as systems engineering approaches that integrate work design with system development; (3) socio-technical systems are best engineered through a combination of constructive engagement and sensitization and awareness; (4) constructive engagement is best understood as the integration of socio-technical systems with existing systems and engineering approaches;
socio-technical systems can be engineered by using a pragmatic approach based on constructive engagement.

socio-technical systems are more effective, efficient and acceptable than systems that are not socio-technical, that socio-technical systems can be developed in a cost-effective manner, and that socio-technical system engineering can be successfully integrated with existing systems and engineering approaches.

the practical application of socio-technical approaches, and the development of a new socio-technical systemsengineering approach to system development.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the adoption of socio-technical approaches is not just a matter of using design methods, but rather a matter of developing a socio-technical culture within organisations.
socio-technical approaches can be applied in a pragmatic way to deliver systems which are more acceptable to users and stakeholders, and which are easier to integrate and maintain.
socio-technical systems can only be developed effectively if the social and technical aspects are addressed in a coordinated way throughout the development life cycle.
